judged_text: The duplicate-attendee guard compares guest emails to existing attendees with exact case-sensitive equality while the schema does no normalization, so the same mailbox can be added repeatedly in different cases. Re-adding 'user@x.com' when 'User@x.com' is already an attendee creates a duplicate attendee row (the dedupe check misses), and the case-sensitive blacklistedGuestEmails check at line 73 sits on the same unnormalized value — every future control layered on these emails inherits the same normalization drift; the next change (e.g. seat-count checks or per-attendee limits) gets riskier because email identity is stored in inconsistent case.

Re-adding 'user@x.com' when 'User@x.com' is already an attendee creates a duplicate attendee row (the dedupe check misses), and the case-sensitive blacklistedGuestEmails check at line 73 sits on the same unnormalized value — every future control layered on these emails inherits the same normalization drift; the next change (e.g. seat-count checks or per-attendee limits) gets riskier because email identity is stored in inconsistent case.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the dedupe/guard logic is case-sensitive: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and the blacklist check is `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` even though the blacklist is lowercased. Since neither the schema (`z.string().email()`) nor the handler normalizes emails (e.g., `toLowerCase().trim()`), the same mailbox can be added multiple times with different casing (e.g., `User@x.com` vs `user@x.com`), creating duplicate attendee rows via `createMany` and bypassing the blacklist depending on case.
